root_cause.text: In the BPF cgroup storage map iterator, cgroup_storage_get_next_key() incorrectly used a NULL check after list_next_entry() for end-of-list detection even though Linux list_next_entry() wraps to the list head instead of returning NULL, causing traversal past the last real element and exposure of bogus internal data as a key.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (!storage)` to `if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that “list_next_entry() never returns NULL,” so the old check was dead code and the function “never returns -ENOENT for the last element, instead reading storage->key from a bogus pointer that aliases internal map fields and copying the result to userspace.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix cgroup storage key iteration to correctly detect the end of the list by checking for the list head sentinel instead of NULL.
intent_record.what: The null check after assigning `storage = list_next_entry(storage, list_map);` was replaced with a call to `list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map)` to detect whether iteration reached the list head.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes end-of-list detection from an ineffective null-pointer check to an explicit check for the list head sentinel used by the kernel list API, so the function correctly returns `-ENOENT` when there is no next key instead of treating the list head as a valid entry or continuing with invalid iteration state.

candidates.rationale: This NULL check is the direct root cause: list_next_entry() does not return NULL at the end of the list, so using this condition for termination fails and allows iteration to advance to the list head sentinel and expose invalid internal data as a key.

This advances iteration using list_next_entry(), whose semantics require explicit checking against the list head sentinel rather than NULL; paired with the subsequent NULL check, it leads directly to traversing past the last real element.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs end-of-list detection using a NULL check, but after advancing with list_next_entry() the Linux list API wraps to the list head sentinel rather than returning NULL. As a result, this condition fails to stop iteration at the end of the real elements, causing traversal into sentinel/internal data and exposure of an invalid key.

This statement advances iteration with list_next_entry(), whose semantics require checking whether the resulting element is the list head sentinel. In combination with the following NULL-based termination check, it causes iteration to move past the last valid storage entry and treat non-element internal list state as a key source.
